module.title: Recursion & the Call Stack
module.subtitle: How a function calling itself builds and unwinds stack frames
lesson_points: Recursion happens when a function calls itself with a smaller input until it hits a stopping condition.
Every recursive function needs a base case (when to stop) so it doesn't loop forever.
Each nested call gets its own fresh local variables on the Call Stack, then unwinds back up on return.
module.example_code:
def sum_down(n):
    if n <= 1:
        return n
    rest = sum_down(n - 1)
    return n + rest

total = sum_down(4)
print("Sum:", total)

quizzes.title: Explain the Base Case
quizzes.prompt: Why does every recursive function require a base case before calling itself again?
quizzes.sample_explanation: The base case tells the function when to stop calling itself so the call stack can unwind instead of repeating forever.
quizzes.explanation: Without a stopping base case, recursive calls pile onto the Call Stack until Python raises RecursionError.
